# Structural results for Enriques and Coble surfaces

## Main results

::: {.theorem #thm:torelli title="Torelli for Enriques"}
Two complex Enriques surfaces are isomorphic if and only if their period
points agree in the quotient of the type IV domain by the stable orthogonal
group of the Enriques lattice.
:::

::: {.proof #thm:should-not-index}
Combine the strong Torelli theorem for the covering K3 surface with the
description of the Enriques involution on the second cohomology lattice.
:::

::: {.lemma #lem:kodaira:embedding}
Every Kodaira fiber type that embeds isometrically into the Coble lattice
does so with primitive image, and any two primitive embeddings of the same
type are conjugate under the Weyl group.
:::

::: {.proposition #prop:fibration-count}
An unnodal Enriques surface carries exactly $527$ isomorphism classes of
elliptic fibrations up to the action of its automorphism group.
:::

::: {.corollary #cor:automorphism-index}
The automorphism group of a very general Enriques surface has index
$$ [O^{+}(E_{10}) : W_{2}(E_{10})] = 2^{21} \cdot 3^{5} \cdot 5^{2} \cdot 7 \cdot 17 \cdot 31 $$
in the orthogonal group of its numerical lattice.
:::

::: {.definition #def:halphen-pencil}
A Halphen pencil of index $m$ is a pencil of plane curves of degree $3m$ with
nine base points of multiplicity $m$, generically an elliptic pencil.
:::

::: {.remark #rmk:characteristic-two}
In characteristic two the period-theoretic argument fails: classical and
supersingular Enriques surfaces admit no crystalline Torelli statement yet.
:::

::: {.example #ex:coble-surface}
The blowup of the plane in the ten nodes of a rational sextic is a Coble
surface; its anti-bicanonical curve is the strict transform of the sextic.
:::

::: {.conjecture #conj:borcherds-form title="Modularity of the Borcherds form"}
The restriction of the Borcherds automorphic form $\Phi_{12}$ to every
Heegner divisor of the Enriques period domain vanishes with known
multiplicity determined by the root invariant.
:::

::: {.claim #clm:isotropic-vector}
Every isotropic vector of the Coble lattice is equivalent, under the group
generated by reflections in $(-2)$-classes, to a primitive one.
:::

::: {.observation #obs:root-invariant}
The root invariant of a nodal Enriques surface refines the count of smooth
rational curves and is constant in equisingular families.
:::

::: {.question #qst:moduli-compactification}
Does the Baily–Borel compactification of the Enriques moduli space admit a
modular interpretation by stable pairs of Halphen type?
:::

::: {.problem #prob:classify-actions}
Classify the finite groups acting semi-symplectically on Coble surfaces of
Halphen index two, together with their fixed-point lattices.
:::

::: {.assumption #ass:very-general}
Throughout, the marked surface is very general: its transcendental lattice
admits no extra algebraic classes beyond those forced by the marking.
:::

::: {.warning #warn:signature-convention}
We use the geometric signature convention $(1, 9)$ for $E_{10}$; sources in
the arithmetic literature often negate the form, which flips every
inequality involving $q(x)$.
:::

::: {.exercise #exr:compute-discriminant}
Compute the discriminant group of $U \oplus E_8(2)$ and verify that it is
$2$-elementary of length eight.
:::

::: {.theorem #thm:}
This near-miss has an empty key and therefore defines no reference target.
:::
